## F082 the rules a member agrees to before publishing a Page (create-posts): 9 of 9

- Can: A member becomes a creator by completing one step before publishing a Page, and takes it again before every new Page; creator status derives from the agreement 
- Can: The step is fixed statements presented as rules with the reason for each, agreed to; nothing typed, no free text stored; no document upload, ID, selfie, photo, 
- Can: Nothing attested renders to peers as a badge, tier, score, label or public claim
- Can: The step gates publishing each new Page, not creating it, selling and hosting alike; creating and editing a draft never asks; browsing, responding, following an
- Can: No string in the step asks the member to classify themselves as a business, uses legal or tax language, or asks for legal-entity information
- Can: The rules are versioned: a member who agreed to an earlier version agrees again before they next publish; each agreement is recorded with version and timestamp,
- Can: The rules are viewable with one click, whether or not the member is taking the step
- Can: Publishing a Page requires a name, a location (address or area) and a description, with the rules agreement and at least one tag; a photo is optional and a Page
- Can: One of the rules is the photo rule: the member agrees not to post pictures of children (draft wording, versioned like the rest)

## F099 every post shows a picture, and every Page can have a Page picture (create-posts): 13 of 14

- Can: Every Page, of every kind, may set one optional Page picture: same field, flow and copy for every kind; a Page without one publishes and shows as today
- Can: A Page with no Page picture shows its kind's placeholder image, identical on every load, to every viewer
- Can: A post may carry one photo of its own; the composer completes without one; a second is refused
- Can: A post's photo belongs to that post only; it does not appear on the Page as a Page photo
- Can: The Page picture and a post photo use the existing upload path: WebP only, metadata stripped, the uploader's own folder, 5 MB at most, verified against the stor
- Can: Every post card shows exactly one image on its Page, in browse and on Home: the post's visible photo, else the Page's visible Page picture, else the kind placeh
- Can: Visible means neither hidden nor removed, resolved in SQL, so a hidden or removed URL does not reach the browser and the card falls to the next image
- Can: The Page picture and each post photo are reportable on their own; a report hides that one image only, and the poster's notice names which
- Can: Adding either image shows the sensitive-content ask at the moment of upload
- Can: Every rendered image has alt text: Page picture and placeholder, the Page's name; post photo, the owner's words, else the default from title, date and place
- Can: Signed out (F093), no post photo is in any response
- Can: Removing either image records an event, and it stops showing on every surface on the next load
- Can: A Page's current photo stays its photo, shown where it shows today; the Page picture starts empty, so the placeholder shows on its posts until the owner sets on
- Cannot yet: The Page picture or placeholder shows wherever the Page's name does, and the withheld card is unchanged

## F078 flagged content hides itself, and the poster is told why (moderation): 12 of 13

- Can: Anything a member can post is reportable (photos, Pages, announcements, posts); a report triggers agent classification
- Can: A first report leaves the post up and sends a courtesy notice; a second report from a different member hides it and sends it to a person
- Can: Poster told at once, in-app (never email), with the category, the reporter's reason and a plain explanation
- Can: The poster can submit one explanation; an unanswered takedown stays hidden and closes itself
- Can: Threat of harm or children texts Don at once; everything else queues in a mobile review view
- Can: Every report lands in the same queue, whether or not it hid anything
- Can: The hide bar stays per-metro data, no migration or deploy; zero at launch; unresolved metro uses zero
- Can: A Threat of harm or Sensitive content report hides at once, on the first report, at any bar
- Can: A report cannot be sent without a reason the reporter chose
- Can: Before sending, the reporter is told misuse has consequences; rejected reports are strikes and after three stop hiding
- Can: Every string in the report path is kind and gracious; wording is Don's
- Can: The second report that hides an item must come from a different member than the first
- Cannot yet: Submitting an explanation is the only thing that creates work for a person

## F100 an AI reads every reported item first, and a person makes the call (moderation): 11 of 13

- Can: Every report and every poster rebuttal triggers one AI assessment, after the report is stored and hidden
- Can: First pass is Claude Haiku, text and vision, structured output
- Can: Below 0.70 confidence Sonnet gives a second opinion; both reads stored, the shown one is the second
- Can: Only the content, the reporter's reason and the rebuttal are sent; no name, handle or email; rules text versioned
- Can: Each assessment stores model, prompt version, category, severity, confidence, outcome, reason, latency, time; RLS on, no policies
- Can: Shadow mode: an assessment changes nothing (save F102's severity-4 restore)
- Can: When a person decides, agreement is logged
- Can: Live mode is a data switch; live raises a row's severity and order; remove, restore, strikes stay a person's tap
- Can: An evaluation harness prints recall, false alarms, severity accuracy, latency and cost; it runs on every prompt change
- Can: Builder agents build the labelled set: licensed photos, a children-rule case, an adult case, no minors in sensitive context
- Can: Beta half of 11: the PM sees recall, severity-1 recall, false alarms and shadow days against the targets
- Cannot yet: Production half of 11: software refuses the live flip until a passing harness run and the shadow read are recorded
- Cannot yet: Suspected severity-1 content is never sent to an AI provider; images are hash-checked first (Cloudflare) and go to a person with the result
